Report_ID: Pain severity in the previous seven day period
Title: Mobilisation with movement and exercise, corticosteroid injection, or wait and see for tennis elbow: randomised trial
Author: Bisset et al.
Comment: Pain-outcome-specific analysed n was not reported in Table 2, so randomised arm sizes from Table 1 were used as required by the synthesis contract. Endpoint means and SDs are recorded verbatim on the paper's 0–100 mm VAS. M_diff was computed as physiotherapy minus wait and see: 33.8 − 51.0 = −17.2 mm; for synthesis on a 0–10 scale, divide both means, both SDs, and this MD by 10 (giving MD −1.72). The paper separately reports a model-based 'difference in improvement' of 15.6 (99% CI 4.7 to 26.4), oriented so that a positive score favours physiotherapy; this was not substituted for the requested endpoint means/SDs.
Design Type: Pragmatic single-blind three-arm parallel-group randomised controlled trial

Recruitment source: Volunteers from the greater Brisbane region responding to advertisements and media releases
Outcome measurement: Visual analogue scale for pain severity during the previous seven day period, from 0 mm (no pain) to 100 mm (worst pain imaginable)

additional_group_ns: Corticosteroid injection: n=65 randomised; excluded because it is an ineligible drug/injection comparator for this synthesis.

Title: Steroid injection therapy is the best conservative treatment for lateral epicondylitis: a prospective randomised controlled trial
Author: J. H. Tonks, S. K. Pai, S. R. Murali
Comment: Change scores were used because endpoint means and SDs were not reported. The paper does not state the pain-specific analyzed n by arm; per the synthesis contract, randomized arm sizes (12 per arm) were used. The Discussion reports five dropouts from the physiotherapy-alone arm, so this fallback n exceeds the known completer count; the observation-arm follow-up count is only available in Figure 1 and is not stated in the supplied text. The reported p=0.27 is from the factorial ANOVA physiotherapy main effect, not the clean physiotherapy-alone versus observation contrast, so it was not entered as this row's p-value. M_diff and SE_diff were left null because this is a four-arm factorial trial and the extraction rules prohibit computing M_diff as though it were a simple two-group design.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Physiotherapy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Title: Corticosteroid injections, physiotherapy, or a wait-and-see policy for lateral epicondylitis: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Smidt et al.
Comment: Endpoint means were not reported; change/improvement scores were used for both arms. Pain-specific analysed n was not stated, so randomized arm sizes from the Table 3 headers were used, as required by the synthesis plan. The paper reports improvement, where a larger positive value favors physiotherapy; to express the requested pain MD as treatment minus control with lower pain favorable, invert the sign and divide by 10 when harmonizing to the 0–10 scale. Thus, the paper-reported 6-point improvement difference corresponds by prespecified transformation to a pain MD of -0.6 on the 0–10 scale, but the extracted numeric fields retain only the paper's verbatim reported values. The reported 95% CI for the improvement difference is -2 to 14. No outcome-specific final analysed n was explicitly stated.
Medium: Physiotherapy delivered in person with home exercise equipment and instructions
interaction_type: Clinician-delivered physiotherapy and home exercise versus family-doctor wait-and-see advice
Participant type: Adults aged 18–70 years with lateral epicondylitis of at least 6 weeks' duration
Recruitment source: Patients referred by 85 participating family doctors
Outcome measurement: Change/improvement in patient-rated pain during the day, originally assessed on an 11-point numerical rating scale and reported after transformation to a 100-point scale
additional_group_ns: Corticosteroid injection: n=62 (ineligible active drug comparator); reported 6-week pain-during-day improvement 47 (20).

Title: Corticosteroid or placebo injection combined with deep transverse friction massage, Mills manipulation, stretching and eccentric exercise for acute lateral epicondylitis: a randomised, controlled trial
Author: Olaussen et al.
Comment: Table 3 does not state pain-specific analyzed n, so randomized arm sizes from Table 1 were used as required by the synthesis plan. Raw endpoint values are reported on the paper's 0–100 mm VAS: control 44 (SD 25), physiotherapy 45 (SD 23).
